title: Potato Salad
subtitle: New potatoes with a creamy mustard-and-chive dressing
excerpt: New potatoes boiled until just tender, then dressed while still warm with mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, and plenty of chives. The potatoes absorb the dressing better warm than cold.

recipe.sourceNotes: Potato salad is one of the most widely made salads in British, American, and German home cooking. The British version typically uses waxy new potatoes (Jersey Royals in season, Charlotte or similar varieties at other times) dressed in mayonnaise with Dijon mustard and fresh chives. Dressing the potatoes while they are still warm is the key technique: warm potatoes absorb the dressing rather than being coated by it, which gives a better result.

content.text: Dress the potatoes while they are still hot from the pot: the heat opens the potato's surface and allows the dressing to be absorbed rather than sitting on top. A small amount of white wine vinegar added while the potatoes are hot sharpens the overall flavour before the dressing goes on.
Put the potatoes in a large saucepan and cover with cold salted water. Bring to the boil and cook for 15 to 18 minutes until tender when pierced with a knife. Drain well.
While the potatoes are still hot, tip into a large bowl and sprinkle with the white wine vinegar and a pinch of salt. Toss gently. Leave for 5 minutes while the vinegar absorbs.
Mix the mayonnaise, crème fraîche, and Dijon mustard together. Pour over the still-warm potatoes. Toss gently to coat. Add the chives and spring onions. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve warm or at room temperature. The salad can be made up to 2 hours ahead; do not refrigerate or the potatoes will become firm.
